description: Drafts an obituary from details the family gives, the same as Tribute Paper's free obituary writer. Returns three drafts: a traditional obituary (for a funeral home website or newspaper), a warmer personal one, and a short death notice, each with its word count. It never invents anything: a sentence appears only when its detail was given. Ask the family gently for what they'd like included first (the full name and pronoun are needed; dates, family, work, what they loved and the service details make it fuller). Give dates as YYYY-MM-DD.

death_place.description: Where they died, e.g. "at home" or a hospital's name.

donations.description: A charity for gifts in their memory, e.g. "the Lake Superior Literacy Project".

faith.description: Their faith or community, e.g. "was a lifelong member of Hillside Lutheran Church".

full_name.description: Their full name, e.g. Margaret Ellen Lindgren.

funeral_home.description: The funeral home making the arrangements.

gatherings.description: Visitation, burial or reception, in the family's words.

interests.description: What they enjoyed, e.g. "quilting, long walks by the lake, the Sunday crossword".

known_as.description: The name they went by, if different, e.g. Peggy.

loved.description: What they loved most, e.g. "summers at the family cabin".

parents.description: Their parents' names, e.g. Carl and Ruth Halvorsen.

passing.description: How they passed, only if the family wants it said: peacefully, suddenly, long-illness, short-illness.

preceded_by.description: Who died before them, one per line or separated by semicolons.

pronoun.description: The pronoun to use for the person who died. Ask the family rather than guessing.

region.description: Where it will be read, which sets how dates and times are written: us (United States), ca (Canada), uk (United Kingdom or Ireland), au (Australia or New Zealand).

remembered.description: What they will be remembered for, e.g. "her patience and her blueberry pie".

residence.description: Where they lived, e.g. Duluth, Minnesota.

served.description: Military or community service, e.g. "served in the U.S. Navy during the Korean War".

service_city.description: The town or city of the service.

service_kind.description: The kind of service: funeral, memorial, celebration (celebration of life), mass (funeral Mass), graveside.

service_venue.description: Where the service will be, e.g. Hillside Lutheran Church.

spouse.description: Their husband, wife or partner's full name.

spouse_living.description: false if the spouse died before them.

spouse_role.description: What the spouse was to them: husband, wife or partner.

survived_by.description: Who survives them besides the spouse (a living spouse is added from "spouse"), one per line or separated by semicolons, e.g. "her children, Karen (Mark) Olson and David Lindgren; five grandchildren".

work.description: Their work, in the family's words, e.g. "worked as a school librarian for 34 years".

name: write_obituary
title: Write an obituary
